title: Compile material and fluid properties and system parameters
action: Obtain the temperature-dependent Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, and thermal conductivity of bismuth telluride from the literature and implement interpolation/fitting functions. Obtain temperature-dependent property correlations for water and Therminol VP-1. Set the system geometry (collector length 1 m, tube and glass envelope diameters, TEG dimensions) and operational parameters (optical efficiency 0.8, emissivity 0.14, 3175 p-n pairs, insolation 1000 W/m², ambient temperature 20°C, mass flow rates 0.4 and 0.8 kg/s) from the paper.
description: Preparation step to gather all physical property data and fixed parameters needed for the simulation.

title: Solve HSTEG energy balance for all required configurations
action: Implement the energy balance equations (radiation, convection, heat absorption, TEG efficiency and power) for the bare (B‑HSTEG) and vacuum‑enclosed (V‑HSTEG) designs. Solve the coupled nonlinear system iteratively for the following parameter sweeps: (1) concentration ratio C=1–135 with temperature‑dependent bismuth telluride properties; (2) C=1–135 with water HTF, inlet temperature 20°C, mass flow 0.8 kg/s; (3) C=1–135 with Therminol VP‑1, inlet 20°C, mass flow 0.8 kg/s; (4) ZT=0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 at C=25, inlet 20°C, water, mass flow 0.8 kg/s; (5) cold‑side inlet temperature 20‑90°C at C=25, ZT=1, water, mass flow 0.4 kg/s. For every configuration record the hot‑side and cold‑side temperatures (T_H, T_C) and the derived quantities: ΔT, effective ZT, heat losses, electrical power, electrical efficiency, thermal efficiency. Save all results (for both B‑HSTEG and V‑HSTEG) in a structured intermediate file (e.g., JSON or HDF5) that later steps can read.
description: Core numerical simulation that solves the energy balance for every required parameter combination and stores the complete set of computed temperatures, powers, and efficiencies.

title: Write ΔT and ZT versus concentration ratio CSV
action: Extract the ΔT and ZT data for both B‑HSTEG and V‑HSTEG from the simulation results and write the CSV file with columns: C, T_H_B, T_C_B, Delta_T_B, ZT_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, Delta_T_V, ZT_V. Include at least the concentration ratios C=1,5,25,55,95,135 and optionally a finer grid.
description: Scored artifact containing the temperature difference and figure of merit as functions of concentration ratio. The checker recomputes ΔT and ZT from the provided hot‑ and cold‑side temperatures and compares trends and values to the paper.
output_schema: CSV with columns: C (concentration ratio), T_H_B, T_C_B, Delta_T_B, ZT_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, Delta_T_V, ZT_V. All temperature columns in °C, ZT dimensionless.

title: Write heat loss and electrical power versus concentration ratio CSV
action: Extract the heat loss and power data from the simulation results and write the CSV file with columns: C, T_H_B, T_C_B, Q_loss_B, P_TEG_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, Q_loss_V, P_TEG_V. Include values at C=1,5,25,55,95,135.
description: Scored artifact reporting total heat loss and electrical power generated by the TEG for B‑ and V‑HSTEG as a function of concentration ratio. The checker compares the reported values to the paper's numbers (within tolerances) and can recompute energy balance closure from the temperatures.
output_schema: CSV with columns: C (concentration ratio), T_H_B, T_C_B (hot and cold side temperatures for B‑HSTEG, °C), Q_loss_B (W), P_TEG_B (W), T_H_V, T_C_V, Q_loss_V, P_TEG_V.

title: Write efficiency versus concentration ratio (water HTF) CSV
action: Extract the efficiency data for water as HTF (Tcfi=20°C, mdot=0.8 kg/s) and write the CSV file with columns: C, T_H_B, T_C_B, eta_elec_B, eta_th_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V. Include values at C=1,5,25,55,95,135.
description: Scored artifact for electrical and thermal efficiencies as functions of concentration ratio when using water as the heat transfer fluid. The checker compares the efficiencies to the paper's Table 2 values and verifies trends.
output_schema: CSV with columns: C (concentration ratio), T_H_B, T_C_B (°C), eta_elec_B (fraction), eta_th_B (fraction), T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V.

title: Write efficiency versus concentration ratio (Therminol VP‑1) CSV
action: Extract the efficiency data for Therminol VP‑1 (Tcfi=20°C, mdot=0.8 kg/s) and write the CSV file with columns: C, T_H_B, T_C_B, eta_elec_B, eta_th_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V. Include values at C=1,5,25,55,95,135.
description: Scored artifact for electrical and thermal efficiencies as functions of concentration ratio when using Therminol VP‑1. The checker compares the efficiencies to the paper's reported values and trends.
output_schema: CSV with columns: C (concentration ratio), T_H_B, T_C_B (°C), eta_elec_B (fraction), eta_th_B (fraction), T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V.

title: Write efficiency versus ZT CSV
action: Extract the efficiency data for the ZT sweep (C=25, Tcfi=20°C, water, mdot=0.8 kg/s) and write the CSV file with columns: ZT, T_H_B, T_C_B, eta_elec_B, eta_th_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V. Include ZT values 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0.
description: Scored artifact reporting efficiencies as functions of the thermoelectric figure of merit (constant ZT). The checker compares the efficiencies to the paper's Table 2 values and verifies the monotonic trends.
output_schema: CSV with columns: ZT (dimensionless), T_H_B, T_C_B (°C), eta_elec_B (fraction), eta_th_B (fraction), T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V.

title: Write efficiency versus cold‑side inlet temperature CSV
action: Extract the efficiency data for the Tcfi sweep (C=25, ZT=1, water, mdot=0.4 kg/s) and write the CSV file with columns: Tcfi, T_H_B, T_C_B, eta_elec_B, eta_th_B, T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V. Include Tcfi = 20,30,40,50,60,70,80,90 °C.
description: Scored artifact reporting efficiencies as functions of the cold‑side fluid inlet temperature. The checker compares the efficiencies to the paper's reported trend and values.
output_schema: CSV with columns: Tcfi (°C), T_H_B, T_C_B (°C), eta_elec_B (fraction), eta_th_B (fraction), T_H_V, T_C_V, eta_elec_V, eta_th_V.
